HERITAGE CONTENT ACCESS LICENCE (HCAL) — Version 1.1
Heritage Scripture Server Platform
Issued: 2026-05-11

PREAMBLE
Sanskrit heritage texts — their source verses, classical commentaries, and the
interpretive works that have grown around them — span many centuries and many kinds of
authorship. Some are ancient compositions whose authors passed millennia ago. Others are
translations, commentaries, and scholarly renderings produced within living memory,
with active copyright held by individual authors or publishers.

The Heritage Scripture Server ("the Platform") respects both kinds of authorship. It
distinguishes clearly between content that is freely redistributable via its API and
content that the Platform holds only under a special, non-transferable reading permission
granted by the copyright holder. This licence sets out those distinctions and the
obligations that follow from them.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 1 — CONTENT TIERS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

All content on the Platform falls into one of three tiers:

TIER A — PUBLIC DOMAIN CONTENT  (freely redistributable, no restriction)
  · Moolam — the Sanskrit source verses. These are ancient compositions. No modern
    copyright attaches to the texts themselves.
  · Transliterations — representations of the moolam in other scripts (Devanagari,
    IAST, Tamil, Telugu, etc.), derived mechanically from the moolam.

TIER B — OPEN CLASSICAL & OPEN DERIVATIVE CONTENT  (API-accessible under HCAL)
  · Sanskrit-language bhāṣya — classical commentaries written in Sanskrit (e.g.
    Śaṅkarācārya's Gītā-bhāṣya, Rāmānuja's Śrī-bhāṣya). These are pre-modern
    works; no modern copyright applies.
  · Sanskrit-language translations and upanyāsas — Sanskrit renderings or
    explanatory texts composed in Sanskrit.
  · Sanskrit subcommentaries (vṛtti / ṭīkā) — classical explanatory works on a
    bhāṣya, written in Sanskrit.
  · AI-generated content — translations, commentaries, or commentary translations
    produced by the Platform's LLM pipeline, whether unreviewed (ai_translated),
    reviewed (ai_reviewed), or editorially curated.
  · Community-created content — translations, commentaries, or explanatory works
    contributed through the Platform's collaborative wiki by registered editors
    (source_type: community or editorial).

  Tier B content is accessible via the API under the conditions of Articles 3–5.
  The Platform expects that future AI-generated and community-created works will
  continue to be placed in Tier B unless a specific decision is made otherwise.

TIER C — PLATFORM-LICENSED CONTENT  (readable on platform only — NOT via API)
  · Authoritative translations — translations of the Sanskrit source into modern
    languages (English, Hindi, Tamil, etc.) by named scholars, published works
    whose copyright is held by their authors or publishers.
  · Modern-language commentaries — commentaries in English, Hindi, or other modern
    languages authored within living memory.
  · Commentary translations — translations of a Sanskrit bhāṣya into any modern
    language; these are composite works with separate copyright.

  The Platform hosts Tier C content under a special, non-transferable reading
  permission from each copyright holder. That permission covers display on the
  Platform's website to authenticated readers. It does NOT extend to:
    · redistribution via API
    · bulk download or systematic harvesting
    · reproduction in third-party applications or databases
    · any AI/ML training use

  Readers who wish to engage with Tier C content must visit the Platform directly.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 2 — API ACCESS BOUNDARIES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The public API exposes only Tier A and Tier B content.

Tier C content is technically blocked at the API layer. Attempting to retrieve a
Tier C work via the API will return HTTP 404 with a message directing the reader
to the Platform. This is not a gap or an error — it is the correct and deliberate
boundary.

The source_type field in every API response indicates which tier the content belongs to:
  Tier A: source_type is absent or "primary" (moolam / transliterations)
  Tier B: source_type is one of ai_translated | ai_reviewed | community | editorial
  Tier C (never returned by API): source_type = authoritative

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 3 — PERMITTED USES (Tier A and Tier B content)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  a) You may use Tier A content (moolam, transliterations) for any purpose —
     commercial or non-commercial — without restriction, subject only to general
     attribution courtesy.
  b) You may display Tier B content in non-commercial applications with full
     attribution as specified in Article 5.
  c) You may quote or cite Tier B content in academic, educational, or research
     works with attribution.
  d) You may build non-commercial tools that retrieve and display Tier B content
     via this API, provided attribution is visible to end users.
  e) You may share individual verses or excerpts of Tier B content in personal,
     educational, or devotional contexts.
  f) You may use AI-generated Tier B translations as reference material, provided
     you note their AI origin and do not represent them as authoritative scholarship.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 4 — PROHIBITED USES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  a) No circumvention of Tier C restrictions. You may not attempt to reconstruct,
     scrape, or otherwise obtain Tier C content through the API, screen scraping,
     or any automated means without written permission from the copyright holder.
  b) No commercial use of Tier B content without direct written permission from
     the Platform. The AI-generated and community content in Tier B is made
     available for research and non-commercial application development; commercial
     licensing requires a separate agreement.
  c) No AI/ML training use. Neither Tier B nor Tier C content may be used as
     training, fine-tuning, evaluation, or prompt data for any machine learning
     model without a separate written agreement with the Platform (Tier B) or
     the copyright holder (Tier C).
  d) No removal or alteration of attribution, copyright notices, source references,
     or the _meta watermark block embedded in API responses.
  e) No database reconstruction or systematic harvesting to build a competing
     archive or corpus of Platform content.
  f) No decontextualisation. Do not present content in ways that materially distort
     its original context or misattribute meaning to an author.
  g) No sublicensing, resale, or sharing of API keys.
  h) No misrepresentation of authorship or AI origin. AI-generated translations
     must be labelled as such; they must not be presented as human scholarship.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 5 — ATTRIBUTION REQUIREMENTS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

For Tier B content, every public display must include:
  · The author's name (from the author field in the API response), or for
    AI-generated content, the label field (e.g. "English (AI — gpt-4o)").
  · The source work or tradition, where available (from the work field).
  · The statement: "Accessed via Heritage Scripture Server (hss.example.org)."
  · A reference to this licence: HCAL-1.1 (hss.example.org/license).

For Tier A content (moolam, transliterations), attribution is encouraged but not
legally required given the public-domain status of the texts.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 6 — ENFORCEMENT AND TERMINATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Any violation of this licence immediately terminates your API access rights. The
Platform may revoke API keys without notice and without refund. For Tier C content,
copyright holders retain all independent legal remedies.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 7 — LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

All content is provided "as is". The Platform does not warrant the completeness,
accuracy, or spiritual correctness of any content. It shall not be liable for any
loss or harm arising from reliance on content, including harm from misinterpretation,
misuse, or errors in AI-generated material.

AI-generated translations are machine outputs. They are provided as an accessible
starting point for engagement with the texts, not as authoritative scholarship.
Users should consult human-authored works for serious study.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE 8 — GOVERNING PRINCIPLES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These texts carry responsibility beyond legal compliance. The Sanskrit scriptural
tradition is a living body of knowledge. Authors, commentators, translators, and
platform contributors have each contributed to its accessibility in good faith.

Users are invited to engage in a spirit of respect — for the texts, for the
tradition, for the human and community authors whose work appears here, and for the
purpose of genuine inquiry. The Platform's mission is access with integrity, not
extraction.

texts.name: ब्रह्मसूत्र
texts.description: The Brahma Sūtra of Bādarāyaṇa, whom tradition identifies with Vyāsa, sets out the teaching of the Upaniṣads in four chapters of terse Sanskrit aphorisms, between 545 and 564 of them as the commentators divide them. Its subject is Brahman: the first chapter shows that the Upaniṣads speak of it with one voice, the second answers objections, the third sets out the means and the fourth the fruit, liberation. It is the reasoned member of Vedānta's three foundations, beside the Upaniṣads and the Bhagavad Gītā, and every school of Vedānta, Śaṅkara's, Rāmānuja's and Madhva's among them, wrote its own commentary on it. Its reader is the one who, having studied, asks what Brahman is: athāto brahma-jijñāsā.

texts.name: माण्डूक्यकारिका
texts.description: The Māṇḍūkya Kārikā is Gauḍapāda's Sanskrit verse exposition of the brief Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad: 215 kārikās in four chapters (prakaraṇas). Tradition names Gauḍapāda the teacher of Śaṅkara's teacher. Its subject is the Self, examined through the syllable Om and the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep, with the fourth, turīya, that underlies them. Its purpose is to show that nothing has truly come into being (ajāti), so that the seeker rests in the non-dual. Regarded as the earliest surviving systematic work of Advaita Vedānta and read with Śaṅkara's commentary, it is for one who has studied the Upaniṣads and wants their teaching argued step by step; other schools read the Upaniṣad differently.

texts.name: महाभारतम्
texts.description: The Mahābhārata, traditionally ascribed to Vyāsa, is the longer of the two Sanskrit epics: some seventy-odd thousand verses in eighteen books (parvas). It tells of the feud between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas that ends in the eighteen-day war at Kurukṣetra, and gathers around it myth, genealogy, statecraft, law and philosophy, including works read on their own such as the Bhagavad Gītā. Its subject is dharma, what right conduct is when duties conflict, and its purpose is to teach it through story and argument; one of the two itihāsas, it carries Vedic teaching into example. It is for every reader, and is usually entered through a single parva or episode.

texts.name: योगवासिष्ठः
texts.description: The Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, also called the Mokṣopāya, "the means to liberation", is one of the longest philosophical works in Sanskrit, traditionally ascribed to Vālmīki. In six books (prakaraṇas) the sage Vasiṣṭha teaches the young prince Rāma, who has come home weary of the world. Its subject is the mind and the world it makes; its purpose is liberation while living (jīvanmukti). It teaches almost entirely through long, nested stories, and is broadly Advaitic in outlook, though more imaginative teaching than technical argument. It is for the reader who, like Rāma, has grown dispassionate and asks what is real; its stories are largely self-contained and can be read one at a time.

texts.name: श्रीरामचरितमानस
texts.description: The Rāmcaritmānas, "the lake of the deeds of Rāma", is Gosvāmī Tulsīdās's retelling of the Rāma story, composed in Awadhi in the sixteenth century in seven kāṇḍas of caupāī and dohā verses meant to be sung. Its subject is Rāma's life and character; its purpose is devotion (bhakti) to Rāma and, through it, a guide to living. It draws on the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa but tells the story as an act of love and surrender, moving constantly between narrative and prayer, and belongs to the bhakti poetry of North India that set devotion in the people's own language. It asks of its reader faith and love more than learning, and is recited in homes and in great public recitations.

texts.name: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता
texts.description: The Bhagavad Gītā, ascribed to Vyāsa, is a Sanskrit dialogue of some 700 verses in eighteen chapters, set in the Bhīṣma Parva of the Mahābhārata. As the armies stand ready at Kurukṣetra, Arjuna loses heart and asks Kṛṣṇa to teach him. Its subject is right action and knowledge of the Self; its purposes run from steadying a troubled mind to liberation, and it is recited daily as well as studied. It condenses the teaching of the Upaniṣads and stands with them and the Brahma Sūtra as one of the three foundations of Vedānta, read differently by Śaṅkara, Rāmānuja and Madhva. Its reader is anyone who, like Arjuna, stands between duty and doubt and asks to be taught.

texts.name: श्री राम कृष्ण लीला भक्तामृत चरितावली (भाग १)
श्री राम कृष्ण लीला भक्तामृत चरितावली (भाग २)
सुभाषितसङ्ग्रहः
texts.description: This Subhāṣita-saṅgraha gathers subhāṣitas, "things well said": single Sanskrit verses, each complete in itself, that put worldly wisdom, counsel, wit or observation memorably enough to be repeated. They come from the epics, the fable collections, the poets and the treatises on statecraft and love, and from many anonymous verses whose authors are lost; a verse becomes a subhāṣita by being apt, not by who wrote it. Its subject is life as it is actually lived; its purpose is good counsel, graceful speech and delight. With no story or argument running through it, it is for any reader, to be dipped into by theme or mood rather than read through.

texts.name: श्रीमद्वाल्मीकि रामायणम्
texts.description:
The Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa is the ancient Sanskrit epic (ādi-kāvya) traditionally ascribed to the sage Vālmīki — about 24,000 verses across seven Kāṇḍas: Bāla, Ayodhyā, Araṇya, Kiṣkindhā, Sundara, Yuddha and Uttara. Each Kāṇḍa is divided into Sargas (cantos) and each Sarga into ślokas (verses).

This edition follows the Southern recension and reproduces the digital edition prepared by Rashtriya Sanskrita Vidyapeetham, Tirupati (hosted at valmiki.iitk.ac.in and rsvpramayana.in): the word-order meaning and English translation of every verse, a contemporary-English summary of each Sarga, and six selected classical Sanskrit commentaries together with their English translations.

texts.name: योगसूत्राणि
texts.description: The Yoga Sūtras, compiled by Patañjali in Sanskrit, are some 195 terse aphorisms in four chapters (pādas) that found the Yoga school of Indian philosophy. Their subject is the mind: the second sūtra defines yoga as the stilling of its movements, and the rest sets out the obstacles, the eight limbs of practice, the powers that arise on the way, and freedom (kaivalya), which is the text's purpose. The sūtras assume the Sāṃkhya analysis of spirit and nature, and are so compressed that they have always been read with a commentary, first the Yoga-bhāṣya ascribed to Vyāsa. They are for the practitioner willing to train attention, and are best read slowly, a few at a time.

groups.name: लघुगीताः
groups.description: Aṣṭāvakra · Avadhūta · Kapila · Śri Rāma · Śruti · Uddhava · Vibhīṣaṇa

groups.name: शङ्करग्रन्थसमुच्चयः
groups.description: All works traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya — devotional hymns (stotras) addressed to Devī, Gaṇeśa, Śiva, Subrahmaṇya, Viṣṇu, and miscellaneous deities; preliminary prakaraṇas; and the four comprehensive treatises Upadeśasāhasrī, Vivekacūḍāmaṇi, Prapañcasāra and Sarva-Vedānta-Siddhānta-Sāra-Saṅgraha.

groups.name: सर्वमूलग्रन्थाः
groups.name_en: Sarvamūla — the works of Śrī Madhvācārya
groups.description: The Sarvamūla-granthas: the complete works of Śrī Madhvācārya (Ānandatīrtha, 13th c.), founder of Tattvavāda (Dvaita) Vedānta — his bhāṣyas on the Brahmasūtras, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Upaniṣads; the tātparya-nirṇayas on the Mahābhārata and the Bhāgavata; the ten prakaraṇas; works on conduct and worship; and his hymns. Arranged by prasthāna, as setutila.in arranges them. Entering a text from here reads it through these works alone.

groups.name: नेपाली साहित्य
groups.description: Ten Nepali literary works hosted at the IIT Kanpur Heritage Site (nepali.iitk.ac.in): Bhānubhakta's Rāmāyaṇa (the first Nepali rendering of Vālmīki's epic), Lakṣmīprasād Devakoṭā's narrative verse (Moonamadan, Ritu Vichar, Tarun Tapsi), prose collections by Bhairav Aryal and Lil Bahadur Chettri, and others.

groups.name: श्री राममंगलदास दिव्यग्रन्थसमुच्चयः
groups.description: The devotional corpus of Paramahaṃsa Śrī Rāmmaṅgaladāsajī — the Bhaktāmṛta caritā cycle and related līlā narratives.
